Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Wiki

Wiki — articles the team writes for itself

Write Markdown articles for the people who run the console, file them by topic and tags, publish each one to Global or to chosen ADOMs, optionally limited to profiles and groups; discuss them in comments, follow them, export them as Markdown or PDF and publish them to Confluence.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionswiki.view wiki.write wiki.moderate
📍 WhereOperations → Wiki, the first entry of Operations in every device ADOM and of the Global block (URL /wiki/)

What is it?#

The Wiki holds articles written by the people who run SATOM, for each other: how a certificate is renewed here, why a policy is built the way it is, what to check first when a backend fails. Articles are written in a rich-text editor that stores Markdown, keep every published version, sit in a topic tree and carry free tags and a short description.

Where is it?#

Operations → Wiki, the first entry of Operations in every device ADOM, and the first entry of the Global block in the Global ADOM. In a device ADOM the list opens on that ADOM's articles plus the Global ones; in the Global ADOM it opens on every ADOM.

How to use#

  1. Open Operations → Wiki and click New article in the menu on the left (needs wiki.write). A dialog opens; if something is wrong it says so and keeps what you typed.
  2. Give it a title, a one- or two-sentence Description, and write the text in the editor. Pasted or dropped files are not stored: link an image by its https:// address.
  3. Pick a Topic and type Tags.
  4. In Who can read it, keep Global or tick ADOMs instead, and tick profiles or groups if it is not for everyone.
  5. Changes are saved automatically as a draft only you can see. Press Publish to share it: that is version 1.
  6. Later edits are saved as a draft again; readers keep the published version until someone presses Publish, which makes the next version. What changed (optional) is shown in History. Discard draft drops the unpublished changes.

Finding an article#

The menu on the left of the list and of every article holds New article, Search the Wiki, the topic tree (each topic with the number of articles you can read, sub-topics included) and the tags. A search matches when every word appears somewhere in the title, description, text, tags, author, or the name or description of the article's topic or any topic above it. The list also filters by ADOM (one checkbox per active ADOM plus Global), status, topic, tag and Mine. Below about 520 px of Wiki width the menu moves above the list.

Who can read an article#

The editor's Who can read it card sets the audience. A reader must pass both filters:

Filter Default
ADOMs Global ticked: every ADOM. Ticking an ADOM clears Global; unticking the last ADOM ticks it again
Profiles and Groups nothing ticked: everyone who can see those ADOMs

  • An article that was never published is a draft only its author sees.

  • With profiles or groups ticked, a reader needs one of the profiles or membership of one of the groups.

  • A profile confined to some ADOMs never sees an article published only to other ADOMs, even when that profile is ticked.
  • You can publish only to the ADOMs your own profile reaches.
  • The author always reads their own articles; moderators read every article.
  • An article you may not read does not exist for you: it is not listed or counted, its tags are not suggested, and its address answers not found.
  • Deleting the last profile or group an article was limited to never opens it to everyone: it stays readable by its author and the moderators, and the article says so.

Topics, tags and history#

  • Topic: one per article, in a tree (FortiWeb › Certificates). Filtering by a topic includes its sub-topics. Moderators manage the tree under Wiki → Topics; deleting a topic keeps its articles, without a topic.
  • Tags: comma-separated, stored in lower case (TLS and tls are one tag), suggested as you type from the tags of articles you can read.
  • History: every publication is a numbered version; publishing with nothing new makes none. History on the article lists them and each one reads as it was.
  • Archive on the article takes it out of the default list without deleting it; Restore brings it back.

Editing together#

Anyone with wiki.write who can read an article can edit its title, description, text, topic and tags. Every save carries the draft's revision: if someone else saved the draft after you opened it, your save is refused, autosave stops and the editor says who saved and when. Reload to see their changes; nothing is overwritten. Who can read the article, archiving and deleting stay with its author and the moderators — other editors see the audience fields disabled.

Comments#

Under every published article, Comments holds a threaded discussion.

  1. Type in Add a comment (Markdown, same rules as articles) and press Comment. You now follow the article.
  2. Reply under a comment answers it; replies are indented (five levels on screen).
  3. Edit is for the comment's author; Delete for its author, the article's author and the moderators. A comment with replies becomes Comment deleted. so the thread still reads.

Commenting needs wiki.write and being able to read the article. Archived articles keep their comments, closed; drafts have none.

Following and notices#

Follow on an article, on a topic's list or on a tag's list — or Wiki → Following — puts a notice in your bell when something you follow changes: an article (new versions and comments), a topic (sub-topics included), a tag, an ADOM (its articles and the Global ones), Global, or everything.

  • A notice reaches only people who can open the article when it is sent, never the person who acted. The bell asks again every time it is drawn: an audience narrowed later, or a group or ADOM you lost, takes the notice out of your bell. Deleting an article deletes its notices.
  • Whoever you answered hears replied to you even if they stopped following.
  • E-mail per subscription also mails your recovery address (Settings → Security), when e-mail is enabled: title, description or comment excerpt and the link, never the article text. A sent e-mail cannot be taken back.

Export#

  • Export → Markdown (.md) or PDF on an article downloads its published version; History exports any earlier version. Drafts never leave SATOM.
  • Export on the list downloads a ZIP (Markdown or PDF) of every published article the list shows with its filters, a folder per topic, 500 at most.
  • Markdown keeps the text as written under a YAML header (title, description, topic, tags, audience, version, author, dates, link).
  • The PDF is rendered on the node from the page's safe HTML. Images are not downloaded: SATOM does not fetch an address an author typed; the PDF shows their description and link.

To publish an article to Confluence, see Wiki → Confluence.

Permissions#

Permission Allows
wiki.view open the Wiki and read the articles whose audience includes you
wiki.write create articles; edit the text, topic and tags of any article you can read; change the audience of, archive, delete or publish to Confluence your own; comment
wiki.moderate read, edit and delete every article; manage Topics and the Confluence spaces; delete any comment

The readonly system profile has wiki.view, operator adds wiki.write and admin has all three. A custom profile gets none until an administrator adds them under Profiles.

Groups name people across profiles, such as a team or an on-call rota. They are Administrator → Access → Groups (Users and profiles), shared with Python Studio apps and managed with user management; the Wiki menu links there. Deleting a group an article names leaves the article closed, never open.

Safety#

Raw HTML in an article is shown as text, and links to anything but http, https, mailto, in-page anchors and relative addresses are removed. Do not paste passwords, keys or tokens: everyone in the audience can read the article and every earlier version. Creating, editing and deleting articles, topics and comments, exports and Confluence publications are written to the Audit log.

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Cause and fix
No Wiki entry in the sidebar The profile lacks wiki.view. Custom profiles get none of the Wiki keys automatically: add them under Profiles.
A colleague says the article does not exist They are outside its audience: an ADOM their profile does not reach, or a profile/group they do not have. Or it was never published.
An ADOM is missing from Who can read it Your own profile does not reach that ADOM; a moderator can publish there.
"Its profiles and groups were deleted" on an article Every profile and group it was limited to was deleted. Edit it and pick a new audience; until then only the author and moderators read it.
A link in the text is not clickable Its target is not http, https, mailto, an in-page anchor or a relative address, so it was removed.
New article answers 403 The profile has wiki.view but not wiki.write.
"… saved this draft at … after you opened it" Someone else saved the draft while you were editing. Autosave stopped so their text is not overwritten: reload, then redo your change.
Readers still see the old text after an edit Edits are a draft until someone presses Publish.
The audience fields are greyed out Only the author and Wiki moderators change who can read an article.
Save or Publish fails after an upgrade, in a tab left open Reload the page once so the browser loads the current Wiki script.
No comment box under an article You lack wiki.write, or the article is archived (comments closed) or still a draft.
A notice vanished from the bell You can no longer open the article: its audience changed, you left a group or ADOM, or it was deleted.
No e-mail although E-mail is on You have no recovery e-mail address (Settings → Security), or e-mail sending is disabled under Settings → Email.
Export says there is nothing to export The article was never published: drafts are never exported.
An image is missing from the PDF Images are not downloaded into the PDF; it shows the image's text and link.
Unusual characters show as boxes in the PDF The node has no font with those characters; install DejaVu fonts on the node (fonts-dejavu-core / dejavu-sans-fonts).
Wiki groups link gone Groups moved to Administrator → Access → Groups (needs user management).
